title: ‘Simply wrong’: GOP lawmakers caught LYING about gas prices
summary: Chris Hayes (late April 2026) rebuts GOP senators' claims that gas is falling or cheaper than under Biden, with GasBuddy's analyst on war-driven oil, seasonal refinery effects and why exports don't help consumers.

assertions.quote: up by well over a dollar since the war started.

verdicts.note: Weekly regular gasoline stepped from 3.015 (03/02/2026) to 3.502 (03/09) and 3.990 (03/30), reaching 4.500 by 05/11, a 54% rise over the Feb 2026 pre-war monthly baseline of 2.908, in the same weeks WTI jumped from 64.51 (Feb) to 91.38 (Mar); the timing fits the conflict as the cause, though a price series alone cannot rule out other drivers.

assertions.quote: Gas prices continue to come down. Senator Tim Scott, that is simply not true.

verdicts.note: The national average rose for nine straight weeks after the war began, from about 3 dollars to about 4.40 by early May 2026.
The NSA gasoline index rose 24.9% in March, 11.1% in April and 8.6% in May 2026 (254.887 in January to 396.961 in May), a 56% rise over spring; it only began falling in June (-9.7%).

Weekly regular gasoline rose almost continuously through spring 2026, from 3.015 (03/02) to a 4.500 peak (05/11), a 49% climb, and only turned down in the last weeks of May (4.490, 4.475) and through June (4.305 to 3.831); so the claim is wrong for March-mid May and right only if made from mid-May onward.

assertions.quote: IN APRIL OF 2024, WE WERE AT ABOUT 365. SO WE'RE ACTUALLY ABOVE WHERE WE WERE THEN.

verdicts.note: Gasoline averaged about 3.60 a gallon in April 2024 and about 4.30 in late April 2026; the comparison only works against the June 2022 peak.

Spring 2026 (Mar-May) regular gasoline averaged 4.073 (3.638, 4.103, 4.479), 17.7% above the Biden-period (Feb 2021-Jan 2025) mean of 3.461 and 17.4% below the Biden peak of 4.929 (Jun 2022); April and May 2026 were each above the Biden mean, so gasoline was dearer than the typical Biden-era price, cheaper only than the 2022 peak.

assertions.quote: Gas prices rise quickly, but they often take a long time to go down.

verdicts.note: Asymmetric pass-through (rockets and feathers) is well documented in retail gasoline, with increases passed on within days and declines over weeks.

The quick rise is clear in both shocks (a 0.49 jump in one week, 03/02-03/09/2026, and 02/28-03/07/2022), but the slow fall is not: in 2026 the national average dropped from the 05/11 peak of 4.500 to 3.777 by 07/06 (eight weeks, -16%) about as fast as it rose, before climbing again; in 2022 the fall from 5.006 (06/13) back to the 3.6 pre-spike level took about five months versus three months up.

assertions.quote: rising diesel costs in particular also make everything else more expensive.

verdicts.note: Diesel powers freight and farming, so its cost feeds into shipping and food prices, though fuel is only a few percent of most goods' final price.

assertions.quote: IT'S TERRIFIC FOR REFINERS AND OIL COMPANIES AND IT'S NOT SO TERRIFIC FOR CONSUMERS

verdicts.note: US gasoline prices track global crude benchmarks; domestic producers sell at the world price, so exports rise with it rather than holding pump prices down.

US pump prices moved fully with the global crude shock: regular gasoline rose from 2.908 (Feb 2026) to 4.479 (May 2026), +54%, while WTI rose 58%, repeating the 2022 pattern (+40% gasoline, Feb-Jun); the series show consumers were not shielded but do not themselves state the US net-export position.

assertions.quote: THE CHANGE over to summer gasoline, refineries that are undergoing maintenance before the summer driving season.

verdicts.note: Pump prices typically rise 20 to 50 cents from February to May as refineries do turnarounds and switch to costlier summer blends.

The monthly table shows the seasonal pattern the claim describes: May was higher than January in 15 of the 16 years 2010-2025 (e.g. 2024 3.075 to 3.603, 2019 2.248 to 2.859), but the series cannot separate refinery maintenance and summer-blend costs from demand or crude moves as the cause.
